title: Capacity scenario simulation retrospective — cross-region stress test
summary: Postmortem-style retrospective for the cross-region capacity simulation run on 2026-11-13. We ran a stepped synthetic workload (1x -> 3x -> 5x baseline QPS) across us-west1, eu-central1, and asia-south1 to validate autoscale behavior, KV-cache warmup, and failover paths when preemptible capacity is reclaimed.
notes:
Context:
- Goal: validate autoscaling latencies, cache warmup, and fallback routing under bursty distribution and targeted preemptible reclamation in one region.
- Load profile: baseline 400 rps (mixed short text-gen + 10% long-seq infer), ramp to 1200 rps (3x) for 15m, then 2000 rps (5x) short spike for 5m, followed by steady 600 rps.
- Runner: synthetic-generator v2.1 (weighted routing per region).
Observations (raw):
- us-west1: preemptible node reclaim triggered at 11:12 UTC when load hit 3x. Fallback to on-demand pool worked but there was a 90–140s window of degraded p95 (jump from ~180ms to ~520ms for generation endpoints).
- eu-central1: reached GPU util ~94% during long-seq phase; autoscaler queued new nodes but provisioning lagged ~130s due to cloud provider placement delays. This created token-backpressure and headroom starvation for ~6% of requests (observed as 5xx throttle traces).
- asia-south1: behaved stable, but observed higher p99 for KV cache misses (1.2s) until we ran a targeted prefix-warm job. After warming, p99 reduced to ~420ms.
- Circuit-breaker triggers: small number of client SDKs retried aggressively; our current circuit threshold (85% GPU util) allowed retries that exacerbated the spike.
- Routing policy: smart-routing fallback worked — requests were redirected to nearest compatible variant, but cold-start penalty for 8-bit quantized variants added ~220ms to tail latency.
- Observability gaps: traced timelines show a 2–3s discrepancy between autoscaler event and node-register in the control-plane logs; harder to correlate with app-side traces (missing correlation-id in autoscale events).
- Cost note: using on-demand fallback for ~3 minutes in us-west1 would increase unit GPU cost by ~28% for that window; extrapolate monthly cost if this repeats weekly.
Unresolved oddities:
- One of the test runs showed a repeated pattern of 502s that did not map to any GPU OOMs; suspect edge LB healthcheck flapping and transient iptables rule reapplication during node spin-up. Need deeper packet/log analysis.
- A small subset of requests got routed to an older model variant (v1.9.2) instead of pinned v1.10 in eu-central1 during roll-forward; investigate rollout policy mismatch (route table vs model-catalog tags).
Notes-to-self / rough decisions:
- Lower aggressive retry weight in SDK emulators for next simulation.
- Add correlation-id to autoscaler events and emit to node-join logs.
- Create a short warmup job that runs when autoscaler spins up new instances to pre-populate KV cache for heavy prefixes.
- Experiment with lowering the circuit-breaker threshold to 75% for canary regions and 70% for multi-tenant pools.
- Make scheduled reclaim simulation part of weekly chaos rotation (run different region each week).
